newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen staying out of banking system on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen staying out of banking system on Tuesday.

text.p: The Federal Reserve likely could refrain from any open market desk action during its usual midmorning time Tuesday, analysts said.

"After executing a three-day system repurchase agreement yesterday, the Fed likely will refrain from intervening in the money markets today," said economists at UBS Securities. "However, since yesterday's term operation was not fixed, the Fed may need to perform an overnight system repo tomorrow."

Assuming the federal funds rate trades near or slightly below the 5.25 percent target this morning, there may be significant breakage of yesterday's RP, since the stop out rate was 5.29 percent, said Marc Wanshel, economist at Morgan Guaranty Trust Co.

"If the Fed's pattern of activity this period holds, it's likely to replenish the operation with a small ($2.5 billion or less) two-day RP. However, the Fed's choice yesterday of a breakable operation and a smaller than the one it replaced may be a sign the open market desk senses it has come close to meeting its add need for the period," Wanshel said.
If so, he said the Fed could remain on the sidelines even if a sizable amount of collateral was pulled from Monday's operation.
Fed funds were trading at 5-5/16 percent, slightly above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury desk 212-859-1663))
